text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Zimbabwean government has increased urban school fees by up to 90 percent, rural school fees by 25 percent and boarding school fees by 50 percent with effect from May 1. Deputy Education Minister William Gumbochuma said the increases were aimed at helping the cash-strapped government's cost-recovery programme.

- Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi will today (Friday) officially open Zimbabwe's International Trade Fair in second largest city of Bulawayo, where over 30 countries are exhibiting. The week-long fair ends on Sunday.
- Raw sewage from a blocked sewer in Harare's St. Mary's township is flowing straight into Lake Chivero, one of the capital's four main water reservoirs.

- Zimbabwe's ministry of public construction and national housing built houses for senior government officials, including ministers and some select private individuals, and operated an illegal lending scheme between 1992 and 1995 in which more than Z$90 million in outstanding credits may never be recovered.

- International Monetary Fund (IMF) officials will meet Zimbabwean government officials again in Harare in May to review the southern African state's programme to reduce a government deficit expected to end around 12 percent in the financial year ending in June against a target of 8.5 percent.
